items.name: Self-Signing Company
items.purpose: Rail Charter House receives properly sealed continuity orders that the present board denies issuing. Workers seek a suspension of compulsory transfers, not destruction of the company.
invariants: Acquired evidence is not complete Truth.
No generic prophecy, mind control or corporate monster kill.
Past circulation, injury and exclusion cannot be erased by late settlement.
generationEnvelope: Ordinary descriptions only; fixed evidence, deadlines, power and rights cannot be invented.

canon.entry: After the opening Breach, accept an independent consented mandate.
canon.truth: P7_PRIVATE_COMPANY: recurring charter obligations and reconstruction accounts sustain a bounded legal-person Identity across executives. Continuity orders implement the old stabilization bargain, not a thinking machine or a secret current director.
stakes: On day ten the standing charter routine issues a compulsory transfer schedule unless an arrangement protects the affected workers.
Protect current people while retaining incompatible evidence.
pressures: On day ten the standing charter routine issues a compulsory transfer schedule unless an arrangement protects the affected workers.
routes: Independent community, physical or controlled comparison route
interventions: Secure a worker mandate and dual custody of charter and payroll copies.
consequences: Wages and worker veto protected. Board discretion is constrained.
Compulsory transfer routine is stayed. Ongoing inspection and maintenance duty.
Old obligations get a named custodian. Reorganization and compensation costs.
Retained evidence stays available. Standing transfer routine continues.
canon.eastbankContribution: Independent adopted-instruction and continuing-effect support can establish a local deliberate stabilization policy and its present institutional dependence.
revelationPredicates: No single archive or settlement establishes every predicate.
reentry: Late legal review and retained custody remain available.
Withdrawal does not erase acquired support or clock pressure.
canon.orderSafety: Other Signature completions are not prerequisites.
canon.failureContinuity: Issued transfers remain historical facts; a recall and compensation docket can still change current arrangements.

sources.text: Court-certified emergency charter annex instructs the successor company to keep one workable address and payroll schedule even when surviving household lists disagree.
Worker-held countersigned payroll shows the same continuity clause still funds wages and housing after three changes of directors.

A board-authorized duplicate identifies the reconstruction instruction as an adopted policy rather than a missing clerk signature. Names outside its schedule were sent to review, not counted as settled.
A witnessed sealed-ledger comparison produces the same transfer order without a new executive instruction; the output cites the surviving charter clause.

dispositions.changed: Dual countersignature required; continuity payroll retained.
Charter attached to current consenting offices and maintained records.
Freight operations and household obligations separated without deleting debt.
